notes.text: Switzerland targets housing risk with a sectoral countercyclical capital buffer on mortgage loans financing domestic residential property, first activated in 2013, paused from March 2020 to January 2022 and set at 2.5% of relevant risk-weighted positions since its reactivation, a level confirmed in February 2026 while the broad Basel III buffer stays at 0%. The buffer raises banks' cost of mortgage lending relative to other credit and so leans against the price and leverage effects of low interest rates.

sources.title: Stance of the Basel III countercyclical capital buffer in Switzerland

notes.text: With interest rates falling, the Swiss authorities reported in February 2026 that owner-occupied property prices grew significantly faster than a year earlier and that investment-property prices had more than offset their 2022 to 2023 declines. Price-to-rent ratios rose slightly in all residential segments and loan-to-income ratios signal elevated affordability risks, which the authorities judge imply an elevated risk of correction in the mortgage and residential property markets.

sources.title: Stance of the Basel III countercyclical capital buffer in Switzerland

notes.text: As the spread between fixed-rate and SARON-linked mortgage rates widened, the median repricing maturity of new Swiss mortgages fell from 2.1 years in 2024 to 1.0 year in 2025, according to the SNB, although it rose somewhat for owner-occupied homes and fell for investment and non-residential property. Shorter repricing shifts interest rate risk from banks to borrowers, so a future rise in rates would reach debt service, and buy-to-let valuations in particular, more quickly.

Voters and cantons approved the reform of owner-occupier taxation in September 2025, and the Federal Council has set it to take effect on 1 January 2029: the imputed rental value on owner-occupied homes will no longer be taxed, the maintenance-cost deduction for them ends, and mortgage interest stays deductible only in proportion to rented property, apart from a limited first-time buyer deduction. Removing both the notional income and the interest deduction ends the tax reason to keep mortgage debt outstanding and favours owners with little debt over highly leveraged ones.

sources.title: Bundesrat setzt Abschaffung des Eigenmietwerts auf 2029 in Kraft

notes.text: The Federal Statistical Office's residential property price index (IMPI) is a quarterly hedonic index of owner-occupied single-family houses and condominiums, with subindices for five municipality types, starting in 2017. It is built from transactions financed by the largest mortgage lenders, banks and insurers, so cash purchases are not directly observed and multi-family investment buildings are not yet covered, with an index for them planned for the end of 2027.
